newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan urges Israel to stop settlement work.
newsitem.headline: Jordan urges Israel to stop settlement work.

text.p: Jordan urged Israel on Tuesday to stop work on a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem to help prevent Middle East peace talks from breaking down.

"We regard settlements as a contradiction to international law and to the agreement signed between Israelis and the Palestinians," Information Minister Marwan Muasher told reporters after a cabinet meeting.

"We call upon the Israeli government to reverse its decision if we are to preserve the peace process and if we are to preserve the positive atmosphere that has started to prevail after the signing of the Hebron agreement," Muasher said.
King Hussein of Jordan helped broker a last-minute compromise in January between Israel and the Palestinians on Israel's partial withdrawal from the West Bank town of Hebron.

But Israel's plans to build a settlement at Jabal Abu Ghneim, known as Har Homa in Israel, and its unilateral decision to limit its next withdrawal to just nine percent of West Bank territory angered Palestinians.
Israeli bulldozers began work at Har Homa on Tuesday, surrounded by soldiers to keep Palestinian protesters at bay.

King Hussein, who last week accused Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of pushing the Middle East "towards an abyss of bloodshed", met Netanyahu in Jerusalem on Sunday during a visit to offer condolences to families of Israeli schoolgirls killed by a Jordanian soldier.
Netanyahu made clear after the meeting he would not be swayed from building in Jerusalem.

Under the 1993 Oslo accord between Israel and the Palestine Liberation Organisation (PLO), the future of Jerusalem and the fate of Jewish settlements was to be decided in talks that were supposed to have resumed on Monday.
